title: MJH: a governed AI decision platform

readme.text:
MJH proposes three AI-powered decision-support products built on a shared, governed data and intelligence platform.

The goal is to improve inventory allocation, understand market demand, and source graded trading cards more efficiently. Today, these decisions rely heavily on manual analysis, batch data, and the experience of a small number of employees.

The proposed suite will turn fragmented operational and market data into daily, explainable recommendations.

**Core principle:** AI recommends and explains; authorized MJH employees retain decision-making authority.

### The Three Products

| Product | Primary Purpose | Expected Business Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Allocation & Sell-Through Intelligence | Optimize inventory distribution across Walmart stores and e-commerce channels | Higher sell-through, lower shrink and returns, improved margins |
| Market Trends & Sentiment Intelligence | Monitor external demand, sentiment, prices, and market activity | Faster research, earlier trend detection, better-informed purchasing |
| Secondary-Market Procurement Intelligence | Find and evaluate graded cards across approved marketplaces | Reduced sourcing effort, better acquisition economics, lower procurement risk |

targets.text:
### Proposed Acceptance Targets

| Area | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Allocation data reconciliation | At least 98% of expected daily records reconcile within agreed tolerances for four consecutive pilot weeks |
| Allocation work queue freshness | Available by the agreed cutoff on at least 95% of business days |
| Market insight relevance | At least 70% of reviewed items rated useful by pilot users |
| Market entity precision | At least 95% on the reviewed high-priority pilot set |
| Procurement card and grade matching | At least 95% precision on the approved evaluation set |
| Recommendation safety | No bypass of supply, eligibility, contractual, or approval constraints |
| Procurement safety | No bidding, seller communication, or financial commitments through MVP functionality |

These are proposed acceptance criteria, not achieved results or guarantees.

dbcli.text:
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="allocation-db", description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("migrate", help="create or update tables (safe to run repeatedly)")
    p.add_argument("--schema", help="PostgreSQL schema to migrate (default: the connection's search path)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    load_dotenv(Path(".env"))
    url = Settings.from_env().database_url
    if not url:
        print("missing DATABASE_URL (copy .env.example to .env)")
        return 2
    applied = migrate(url, schema=args.schema)
    for name in applied:
        print(f"applied {name}")
    print("database already up to date" if not applied else f"{len(applied)} migrations applied")
    return 0

api_main.text:
"""``allocation-api``: serve the planner app and its API on 127.0.0.1 (Step 6, P11/P12).

Sign-in is DEV ONLY (pick an actor, no password), so the server never listens beyond this
machine. It serves the built app from ``apps/planner/dist`` when present.
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import uvicorn

from allocation_foundation.settings import Settings, load_dotenv

HOST = "127.0.0.1"


def _app(settings: Settings, static: Path):
    from allocation_foundation.api.app import create_app
    from allocation_foundation.api.auth import LocalActorAuth
    from allocation_foundation.api.ops import OpsReader
    from allocation_foundation.workflow.export_cli import build_exports

    exports = build_exports(settings)
    workflow = exports.workflow
    return create_app(workflow, OpsReader(workflow.metrics, workflow), LocalActorAuth(workflow.metrics.identity.actors),
                      settings.session_key, static, exports=exports)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="allocation-api", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=58000)
    parser.add_argument("--static", type=Path, default=Path("apps/planner/dist"),
                        help="the built planner app (npm run build)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    load_dotenv(Path(".env"))
    settings = Settings.from_env()
    if not settings.session_key:
        print("error: set ALLOCATION_SESSION_KEY in .env (any long random value; it signs the session cookie)")
        return 2
    uvicorn.run(_app(settings, args.static), host=HOST, port=args.port)

scenes.heading: MJH foundation
scenes.subheading: Three decision products on a governed platform.

narration.text: The README frames allocation, market trends, and procurement as the core products.
Each product targets a different decision, but shares the same foundation.
The architecture flows from ingestion to canonical data, metrics, and decisions.
That same layer feeds the app, exports, and planner workflows.

narration.text: The FastAPI app handles sign-in, correlation IDs, and refusal handling.
It also serves the planner app and connects to workflow exports.
The project ships command line tools for database, ingestion, metrics, workflow, and API tasks.
The database command applies migrations, and the API serves locally on 127.0.0.1.
The acceptance targets are strict, with 98%, 95%, 70%, 95%, and 95% thresholds.
Those targets define the pilot bar before the suite expands.
Clone the repository and explore the shared foundation.
Then try the commands and see how the workflow fits together.
